# hyperlite_template (Resource)

A template made from a stopped VM, to deploy VMs from it (`hyperlite_vm.clone.template`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A template copied from a VM (the VM stays, as vSphere's Clone to Template). A running VM is shut down for the copy
# and started again.
resource "hyperlite_template" "golden" {
  name = "debian-golden"
  vm   = hyperlite_vm.base.name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Its name. A change renames it.
- `vm` (String) The VM it is made from. A running VM is shut down for the copy and started again when it stays. Read when the template is made only: a later change of the VM does not reach it.

### Optional

- `force_stop` (Boolean) Stop the VM hard when its clean shutdown did not end within `shutdown_timeout`.
- `keep_vm` (Boolean) `true`: the template gets a copy of the VM's disk and the VM stays (vSphere's *Clone to Template*). `false`: the VM becomes the template and is gone (Proxmox VE's *Convert to template*): do not manage that VM with `hyperlite_vm` too.
- `shutdown_timeout` (String) How long the VM's clean shutdown may take: a running VM is stopped for the copy, then started again (`keep_vm`).

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When it was made.
- `id` (String) The template's name.
- `memory_mb` (Number) Memory of the VM it was made from, in MB.
- `os` (String) Its system, if known.
- `ssh_user` (String) The account its system has, if known.
- `vcpu` (Number) Virtual CPUs of the VM it was made from.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import hyperlite_template.golden debian-golden
```
